## Background (B)

Initiate targeted fluid boluses using 0.9% Normal Saline (avoiding hypotonic fluids due to hyponatremia) and prepare for central venous access and vasopressor support if unresponsive to fluid challenges.
* Airway & Ventilation: Await the urgent ABG/lactate results to evaluate for occult tissue hypoperfusion or metabolic acidosis. Keep the patient nil per os (NPO) due to vomiting and potential airway compromise from neurological decline.

## 2. Diagnostic Prioritization & Critical Rule-Outs

* Neurological Workup: Review the CT Brain immediately to rule out intracranial metastases, leptomeningeal carcinomatosis, or an acute cerebrovascular event causing the unilateral right-sided ptosis, headache, and vomiting. If the CT non-contrast is negative, advocate for a contrast-enhanced MRI.
